question: Who gave the term 'Hindu rate of growth', which referred to as the low growth rate period in the Indian economy?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Raj Krishna**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raj Krishna** coined the term 'Hindu rate of growth' to describe the low annual growth rate of the Indian economy, which averaged around 3.5% from the 1950s to the 1980s.
 
• This term was used to highlight the slow pace of economic development in India during the period of planned economy and socialist policies.
 
• The 'Hindu rate of growth' contrasted with the higher growth rates observed in other developing countries during the same period.
 
• Raj Krishna, an Indian economist, used this term to draw attention to the need for economic reforms and liberalization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Raj Krishna** was a prominent Indian economist and professor at the Delhi School of Economics.
 
• The economic reforms initiated in the 1990s helped India break away from the 'Hindu rate of growth' and achieve higher growth rates.
 
• These reforms included liberalization of the economy, reduction of trade barriers, and encouragement of foreign investments.
 
• The term 'Hindu rate of growth' is often used in discussions on Indian economic history to emphasize the importance of policy changes in achieving economic progress.
